meta.headline: Is gas cheaper now than under Biden? It depends on the month
meta.seoTitle: Is gas cheaper now than under Biden?

dek.text: Regular gas cost less than its Biden-era average through February 2026 and more in every month since March, though it has stayed below the June 2022 peak.

assertions.text: Regular gasoline was below its February 2021 to January 2025 average in January and February 2026.
Regular gasoline was above its February 2021 to January 2025 average in every month from March to September 2026, and below the June 2022 peak.

description.text: Gas cost less than its Biden-era average through February 2026 and more from March on. What the federal price record shows, and how crude moved with it.

assertions.text: Regular gasoline was below its February 2021 to January 2025 average in January and February 2026.
Regular gasoline was above its February 2021 to January 2025 average in every month from March to September 2026, and below the June 2022 peak.

sentences.text: In January 2026 a gallon of regular gas cost well below what it had averaged across Joe Biden's presidency; by spring it cost well above that average.

assertions.text: The national monthly average for regular gasoline in January 2026 was well below its February 2021 to January 2025 average.
In spring 2026 the national monthly average for regular gasoline was well above its February 2021 to January 2025 average.

sentences.text: So which is true now?
The answer turns on which month you call now, and the federal price record shows exactly when it flipped, and how the wider measure of prices compares.

sections.name: question-1
sections.heading: Is gas cheaper now than it was under Biden?

sentences.text: At a cabinet meeting President Trump put the case bluntly: "It was $4 and $5 for a gallon of gas", he said, adding "And now it's probably 225".

assertions.text: Trump said gas had been $4 and $5 a gallon.

quote.text: It was $4 and $5 for a gallon of gas
quote.speaker: Trump

assertions.text: Trump said gas was now probably 225.

sentences.text: A few months later CBS News was describing pump prices as "at their highest point since mid-2022".

assertions.text: CBS News reported that gas prices were at their highest point since mid-2022.

quote.text: at their highest point since mid-2022
quote.speaker: CBS News

sentences.text: The Energy Information Administration's monthly record of regular gasoline, in dollars not adjusted for inflation, puts Biden's term in context: from February 2021 through January 2025 the price averaged $3.46 a gallon and peaked at $4.93 in June 2022.

assertions.text: The national monthly average for regular gasoline averaged $3.46 a gallon over February 2021 to January 2025.
Its highest month in that period was June 2022, at $4.93 a gallon.

sentences.text: Every month of 2025 came in under that average, December lowest at $2.89, though the year was about level with the final months of his term rather than below them.

assertions.text: Every 2025 monthly average for regular gasoline was below the February 2021 to January 2025 average, but about level with October 2024 to January 2025.
qualifications: s08 says 2025 was about level with the last months of the previous term: the gap is against the Biden-era average, not the handover price.

assertions.text: The lowest 2025 monthly average was December, at $2.89 a gallon.

sentences.text: January 2026 was lower again, at $2.81.

assertions.text: Regular gasoline averaged $2.81 a gallon in January 2026.

blocks.caption: Regular gasoline, US national monthly average, dollars per gallon (not adjusted for inflation)

sentences.text: Then the weekly price climbed fast, from $3.02 a gallon in the first week of March 2026 to $4.50 by mid-May.

assertions.text: Weekly regular gasoline was $3.02 a gallon in the first week of March 2026.
qualifications: s12, in the callout, says the price record shows when prices jumped, not why.

assertions.text: Weekly regular gasoline reached $4.50 a gallon by mid-May 2026.
qualifications: s12, in the callout, says the price record shows when prices jumped, not why.

sentences.text: The monthly average has stayed high since: $4.36 in September.

assertions.text: The national monthly average for regular gasoline was $4.36 a gallon in September 2026.

sentences.text: Reporters linked the climb to the war with Iran: MS NOW said gas was "up by well over a dollar since the war started", and NBC News said "it's the war in Iran that's largely causing fuel prices to rise".

assertions.text: MS NOW said gas was up by well over a dollar since the war started.

quote.text: up by well over a dollar since the war started
quote.speaker: MS NOW

assertions.text: NBC News said the war in Iran is largely causing fuel prices to rise.

quote.text: it's the war in Iran that's largely causing fuel prices to rise
quote.speaker: NBC News

sentences.text: What the weekly record establishes is the timing of the jump in March 2026; a price series on its own cannot rule out causes other than the conflict, so the link rests on timing.

assertions.text: The weekly price record shows when gasoline prices jumped in March 2026, but a price series alone cannot rule out causes other than the Iran conflict.
qualifications: This sentence is the limitation: the attribution to the conflict rests on timing.

sentences.text: In October the president made the same argument about crude: "Oil was higher under Biden than it is under Trump".

assertions.text: Trump said oil was higher under Biden than it is under Trump.

quote.text: Oil was higher under Biden than it is under Trump
quote.speaker: Trump

sentences.text: The EIA's crude table says otherwise: West Texas Intermediate averaged $97 a barrel in September 2026, its latest month, and no month of Biden's term was higher except March through July 2022.

assertions.text: WTI crude averaged $97 a barrel in September 2026, the latest month in the table, higher than every month from February 2021 to January 2025 except March to July 2022.

blocks.caption: Crude oil and regular gasoline at the turning points, monthly averages, dollars (not adjusted for inflation)

sentences.text: Read together, the series move in step: both peaked in June 2022, both finished 2025 lower than they began it, and crude went from $64.51 a barrel in February 2026 to $91.38 in March, the month gas jumped.

assertions.text: WTI crude peaked in June 2022, was lower in December 2025 than in January 2025, and jumped in March 2026.
qualifications: s18, in the callout, says co-movement cannot show that policy played no part.

assertions.text: Regular gasoline peaked in June 2022, was lower in December 2025 than in January 2025, and jumped in March 2026.
WTI crude averaged $64.51 a barrel in February 2026 and $91.38 in March 2026.
qualifications: s18, in the callout, says co-movement cannot show that policy played no part.

sentences.text: A guest on PBS NewsHour gave the usual explanation, that the pump price "is set in a global market".

assertions.text: A guest on PBS NewsHour said the price paid at the pump is set in a global market.

quote.text: is set in a global market
quote.speaker: PBS NewsHour

blocks.caption: Gas and crude prices at the same months, side by side.

sentences.text: Prices that rise and fall together fit that explanation, but they cannot show that policy had no part, because policy can move the price of crude itself.

assertions.text: Pump prices moving with crude supports the view that gasoline follows the global oil market, but co-movement cannot show that policy played no part, since policy can move crude itself.
qualifications: This sentence is the limitation: co-movement cannot exclude policy effects on crude.

sentences.text: So the honest answer depends on the date: gas was cheaper than the Biden-era average through February 2026, has been dearer in every month since March, and has stayed below the June 2022 peak throughout.

assertions.text: Regular gasoline was below its February 2021 to January 2025 average in January and February 2026.
Regular gasoline was above its February 2021 to January 2025 average in every month from March to September 2026, and below the June 2022 peak.

sentences.text: Gas, though, is a single price, and the same argument is made about prices in general.

sections.name: question-2
sections.heading: Have prices risen less under this administration than under the last one?

sentences.text: The YouTube channel Squirrelly Economics framed it in totals: "Prices rose about 21% over Biden's 4 years".

assertions.text: Squirrelly Economics said prices rose about 21% over Biden's 4 years.

quote.text: Prices rose about 21% over Biden's 4 years
quote.speaker: Squirrelly Economics

sentences.text: The Bureau of Labor Statistics' consumer price index bears out the totals: it rose 21.4 percent from January 2021 to January 2025, and 6.1 percent from January 2025 to September 2026.

assertions.text: The CPI-U rose 21.4 percent from January 2021 to January 2025.
qualifications: s23, in the callout, says the two periods differ in length; s24 compares equal stretches.

assertions.text: The CPI-U rose 6.1 percent from January 2025 to September 2026.
qualifications: s23, in the callout, says this period is a term still running and much shorter.

blocks.caption: Consumer price index for all urban consumers (CPI-U), index level at each date used in the comparison

sentences.text: Those totals compare a completed term with a term still running, and the second stretch is much shorter than the first.

assertions.text: The January 2025 to September 2026 period is much shorter than the January 2021 to January 2025 period.
qualifications: This sentence is the limitation: the periods differ in length.

sentences.text: Over windows of the current term's length at each end of Biden's term, the index rose 13.5 percent from January 2021 to September 2022 and 4.5 percent from May 2023 to January 2025.

assertions.text: The CPI-U rose 13.5 percent from January 2021 to September 2022.
qualifications: s23 carries the period-length limitation; this is the like-for-like comparison.

assertions.text: The CPI-U rose 4.5 percent from May 2023 to January 2025.
qualifications: s23 carries the period-length limitation; this is the like-for-like comparison.

sentences.text: And the current term's figure is still growing: the twelve-month rate went from 2.4 percent in February 2026 to 3.7 percent in September.

assertions.text: The CPI-U 12-month change was 2.4 percent in February 2026 and 3.7 percent in September 2026.
qualifications: s23 carries the period-length limitation; this sentence shows the current figure is still growing.

blocks.caption: The yearly rate of consumer price inflation in early and late 2026.

sentences.text: So prices have risen more slowly this term than across Biden's term as a whole, though faster than in its last stretch, and by a narrower margin than the totals imply; the index itself cannot say how much of either rise any president caused.

assertions.text: The CPI-U rose at a slower annualized pace from January 2025 to September 2026 than from January 2021 to January 2025, by a smaller gap than the cumulative totals show.
qualifications: s23 carries the period-length limitation; this sentence adds that a price index does not attribute cause.

assertions.text: The CPI-U rose more from January 2025 to September 2026 than from May 2023 to January 2025.
qualifications: s24 gives the equal-length windows; s23 carries the period-length limitation.

sections.name: close
sections.heading: How to check the next price claim

sentences.text: Each answer here came down to the calendar: which month counts as now, and how long a stretch is measured.
When someone says prices are lower, ask lower than when, and over how long; and when the pump price moves, look at what crude oil did that month.
